name: Wealth Management
description: Provision of investment advisory, discretionary portfolio management, private banking, and integrated financial planning services to high-net-worth and mass-affluent clients. The capability encompasses client onboarding, suitability assessment, asset allocation, portfolio construction, custody, reporting, and the ongoing client relationship that justifies a premium over commodity investment execution. It is a regulated activity under FCA COBS and an authorised investment service under MiFID II.
mandate_source: Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (FSMA) — authorised activity
MiFID II / MiFIR (onshored as UK MiFID) — investment advice, portfolio management, and client classification
FCA Conduct of Business Sourcebook (COBS) — suitability, appropriateness, and inducements
FCA Consumer Duty (PS22/9, effective July 2023) — outcomes-based suitability and fair value
FCA Product Governance (PROD) — target market assessment and distribution strategy
FCA Advice Guidance Boundary Review (CP23/24) — proposed 'targeted support' regime
Senior Managers and Certification Regime (SM&CR) — accountable individuals for investment services
FCA Sustainability Disclosure Requirements (SDR) and investment labels (PS23/16)

table_stakes: Discretionary and advisory portfolio management across equities, fixed income, and multi-asset
ISA, GIA, SIPP, and offshore bond wrappers
Suitability assessment and risk profiling at onboarding and periodic review
MiFID II ex-ante and ex-post costs and charges disclosure
Client reporting: valuation, performance, and transaction statements
Dedicated relationship manager for HNW clients (threshold typically £250k–£500k AUM)
differentiators: Integrated banking-and-wealth proposition (deposit, lending, mortgage, and investment on one balance sheet) — a structural advantage traditional wealth managers cannot replicate
Bespoke tax-efficient structuring: trusts, AIM portfolios for BPR, offshore bonds coordinated with personal tax
Intergenerational wealth transfer: estate planning, family governance, philanthropy coordination
Lending against portfolio (portfolio-secured credit) as part of the holistic relationship — not available to standalone investment managers
Proprietary alternatives access: private equity co-investment, structured products, direct lending funds
ESG portfolio integration with authentic stewardship credentials (voting policy, engagement reporting)
disruptors: Nutmeg (JP Morgan): largest UK robo-adviser with ~£5bn AUM; benchmark for digital onboarding, transparent pricing (0.45–0.75% all-in), and mobile-first UX — demonstrates that discretionary management can be delivered at sub-1% cost
Wealthify (Aviva): ISA and GIA from £1; normalised micro-investing and ethical portfolio options at mass-market scale
Moneyfarm: goals-based investing for mass-affluent; digital financial planning integrated with investment management
Hargreaves Lansdown: £150bn+ AUM D2C platform; Vantage ISA/SIPP; sets the benchmark for self-directed clients and is migrating upmarket with advisory services
AJ Bell and Interactive Investor: low-cost D2C platforms compressing fee expectations; ii's flat-fee model disrupts percentage-based pricing for larger portfolios
Vanguard Personal Investor: 0.15% platform fee cap; sets a permanent floor under commodity passive management costs
Saltus, Evelyn Partners, Quilter: consolidating mid-market wealth; rolling up boutiques to achieve scale in regulatory compliance and technology
unbundling: Investment management commoditised: passive ETF execution (iShares, Vanguard, HSBC Asset Management) separates alpha generation from portfolio construction — clients increasingly sceptical that active management justifies the fee delta

Financial planning unbundled from investment: chartered financial planners (CFPs) operating as fee-only advisers using cashflow modelling tools (Voyant, CashCalc, Timeline) without managing assets directly
Platform custody separated from advice: wealth firms increasingly white-labelling FNZ or SEI rather than building proprietary custody infrastructure
Performance reporting unbundled: third-party reporting portals (Wealth Dynamix, InvestCloud) used as client-facing layer over multiple custodians
Tax and estate planning migrating to specialist boutiques and Big Four private client practices
rebundling: St. James's Place, Quilter, and Evelyn Partners re-bundling advice, investment management, and financial planning under one AUM fee — resisting unbundling pressure with face-to-face relationship model
JP Morgan Private Bank re-bundling banking, lending, and investment for UHNW — same structural play as a commercial bank with a wealth arm
Revolut and Monzo extending into investments (Revolut Stocks, UK share-dealing) — bundling investment alongside payments for mass market; not yet a wealth threat but signals direction of travel
switching_drivers: Fee transparency: MiFID II ex-post reporting has made total costs visible; clients compare all-in charges directly against D2C platforms
Relationship manager attrition: wealth is a relationship business; RM departure triggers ~30–40% of book at risk of switching (industry data)
Performance underperformance vs benchmark: sustained underperformance against ARC or WMA indices prompts review
Digital experience gap: clients using Monzo/HL for personal banking expect real-time mobile portfolio access — legacy portals create switching pressure
Life events: divorce, inheritance, business sale trigger re-evaluation of wealth provider

HNW threshold migration: rising living costs and asset inflation pushing the effective HNW entry point toward £500k liquid assets, leaving mass-affluent clients under-served by traditional managers and over-priced for robo

current: UK MiFID (onshored MiFID II): investment advice and discretionary portfolio management are regulated investment services; MiFID II costs and charges transparency requires ex-ante and ex-post disclosure; best execution obligations apply to portfolio management

FCA Consumer Duty (PS22/9, July 2023): outcomes-based regime requires firms to demonstrate fair value in products and services, suitable client outcomes, and comprehensible communications — materially raises the bar for suitability documentation and pricing justification in wealth
FCA PROD: product governance requires target market assessment for advised and discretionary services; distribution strategies must match product to defined client segment

SDR / ESG labels (PS23/16, effective December 2024): funds must use defined sustainability labels (Sustainability Focus, Improvers, Impact, Mixed Goals); greenwashing risk now a named FCA enforcement priority
COBS 9A suitability: periodic suitability reviews required for ongoing advisory and discretionary clients; failure to conduct or document reviews is a recurring FCA enforcement focus
incoming_2_3_years: FCA Advice Guidance Boundary Review (CP23/24 — targeted support proposal): would create a new 'targeted support' category allowing firms to provide more prescriptive guidance to mass-market clients without triggering full regulated advice — potential to democratise the advice funnel significantly and blur boundaries between D2C platforms and advised wealth

FCA Consumer Composite Investments (CCI) regime: successor to PRIIPs/KIDs for UK retail investment products; expected 2025–2026; requires revised disclosure documents for structured products and packaged investments

Open Finance extension to investments: FCA roadmap for data sharing beyond Open Banking to include investment accounts, pensions, and insurance — would commoditise account aggregation and intensify switching
FCA Sustainability Disclosure Requirements Phase 2: extension of SDR labelling and anti-greenwashing rules to portfolio managers and model portfolio services (MPS); expected 2025
Potential MiFID review: HM Treasury consultation on UK MiFID framework may adjust suitability requirements and open new distribution channels
enforcement_signals: FCA Dear CEO letter (January 2023): wealth managers and stockbrokers must demonstrate Consumer Duty readiness; FCA explicitly flagged fair value assessments and suitability processes as priority review areas
FCA DB pension transfer redress scheme (PS22/20): ongoing liability for firms that gave unsuitable DB transfer advice; signals long-tail regulatory risk in historical advice books
FCA enforcement action on inducements (ongoing): host of cases against discretionary managers for undisclosed third-party payments; reinforces MiFID II inducement controls
FCA Retirement Income Review (DP23/3): focus on whether advised clients in decumulation receive suitable drawdown advice — relevant to financial planning sub-capability
FCA anti-greenwashing rule (May 2024): first standalone anti-greenwashing guidance; wealth managers promoting ESG portfolios now subject to direct enforcement risk

platform_options: FNZ: end-to-end platform-as-a-service covering custody, settlement, client portal, and reporting; used by Lloyds Banking Group (Scottish Widows), Standard Life, and HSBC Global Asset Management; strong UK regulatory track record
SEI Wealth Platform: integrated investment management, custody, and reporting; targeted at private banks and wealth managers; used by RBC Brewin Dolphin and Julius Baer
SS&C Advent: portfolio management system (Geneva) and reporting; strong in institutional and family office; less commonly used for mass-affluent
InvestCloud: modular digital wealth platform; client portal, proposal tools, and performance reporting; used by several tier-2 banks as front-end overlay
Wealth Dynamix (WDX): CRM designed specifically for wealth management; workflow for onboarding, reviews, and compliance documentation
BlackRock Aladdin Wealth: risk analytics and portfolio construction engine; used for model portfolio management and risk budgeting
Bloomberg PORT: portfolio risk and performance attribution; used by investment managers for MiFID II performance reporting

Voyant / CashCalc / Timeline: financial planning and cashflow modelling tools; Voyant dominant among UK IFAs; CashCalc strong in adviser-managed plans; Timeline specialised in sustainable withdrawal rate modelling
Objectway / GBST: back-office and settlement for retail investment platforms; less prominent since FNZ consolidation
must_build_in_house: Client relationship model and RM tooling: the commercial bank's relationship model, segmentation logic, and RM performance framework must remain proprietary — this is the core competitive asset

Suitability and KYC orchestration: the workflow that connects client data, risk profile, product governance target market, and regulatory documentation must be owned in-house to ensure Consumer Duty compliance and auditability

Investment Committee process and model portfolio construction: asset allocation decisions, manager selection rationale, and ESG integration policy must be bank-owned for MiFID II accountability and brand differentiation
Integration with core banking balance sheet: the linkage between wealth AUM, deposits, lending, and FX is the structural moat — this integration cannot be outsourced
Regulatory reporting: MiFID II transaction reporting, EMIR derivatives reporting, and SDR label compliance attestation must be bank-controlled
buy_candidates: Platform custody and settlement: FNZ or SEI are strong candidates — building proprietary custody infrastructure is capital-intensive, heavily regulated, and does not create competitive advantage
Portfolio analytics and risk: BlackRock Aladdin Wealth or Bloomberg PORT for risk decomposition and performance attribution — commodity capability with high build cost
Client reporting portal: InvestCloud or SEI digital portal as white-labelled overlay — faster time to market and lower maintenance than bespoke build
Financial planning tools: Voyant or CashCalc for cashflow modelling — strong market penetration among UK advisers and embedded in client workflow
CRM for wealth: Wealth Dynamix (WDX) or Salesforce Financial Services Cloud for RM workflow, review scheduling, and compliance documentation

primary_revenue_streams: AUM-based management fee (typical range 0.5–1.0% p.a. for discretionary; 0.25–0.75% for advisory) — primary revenue driver but under structural compression
Platform/custody fee charged on top of or embedded within the management fee
Financial planning fee: fixed annual retainer or hourly rate for cashflow modelling, retirement planning, and tax structuring — growing as fee transparency unbundles planning from investment
Private banking fees: structured product margins, FX spread on international transfers, mortgage arrangement fees, and credit facility fees
Transactional revenue: dealing commissions (diminishing under MiFID II), fixed income spread on bond execution
Referral revenue from bancassurance: life insurance, protection, and annuity products cross-sold through wealth channel
margin_pressure: MiFID II ex-post cost disclosure directly compares all-in charges against D2C alternatives — clients with £500k+ portfolios increasingly question the fee delta vs Hargreaves Lansdown or Vanguard
Passive ETF penetration: AUM-based fees on passive portfolios are difficult to justify; active management alpha must demonstrably offset the cost delta
Robo-advisory pricing floor: Nutmeg and Wealthify have established a ceiling of ~0.75% all-in for digital discretionary — traditional managers above this level face justification pressure
Regulatory compliance cost escalation: Consumer Duty implementation, SDR compliance, and suitability documentation increase cost-to-serve, particularly for smaller client balances
RM talent inflation: wealth management RMs command premium salaries; wage inflation compresses margin in the advisory and relationship model
Falling platform margins: FNZ and SEI custody fees being re-negotiated down as scale increases; margin shifts to the value-added layer
cross_sell_hooks: Private banking lending: HNW clients with liquid portfolios are prime prospects for portfolio-secured credit, commercial property mortgages, and structured lending facilities

Corporate banking cross-sell: business owners served by corporate banking are natural prospects for personal wealth management; business sale / liquidity event triggers a significant wealth conversion opportunity
Pension and retirement: SIPPs managed on the wealth platform are a gateway to drawdown advice, annuity placement, and intergenerational estate planning

FX and international banking: clients with international assets or income require FX conversion, offshore accounts, and international payment capability — natural upsell within the private banking relationship
Protection and life insurance: cashflow modelling through financial planning exposes protection gaps; referral to bancassurance or broker panel

sub_capabilities.name: Investment Advisory
sub_capabilities.description: Provision of personalised investment recommendations under FCA regulation: conducting suitability assessments, constructing advised model portfolios, and providing periodic review advice. Covers both restricted and independent advice models, and includes the documentation, rationale, and audit trail required under COBS 9A and Consumer Duty.

promotion_test.market_evidence: Investment Advisory shares the same regulated entity, the same FCA permissions, and the same client relationship as Portfolio Management and Private Banking. The market evidence confirms integration rather than separation: St. James's Place, Quilter, and Evelyn Partners all run advisory and discretionary services from a single regulated firm with shared RM, suitability, and compliance infrastructure. The standalone Independent Financial Adviser (IFA) market does demonstrate that advice can be unbundled from asset management — firms like Tilney or 7IM offer advice-only engagements — but in the context of a commercial bank wealth arm, the relationship manager is the advice vehicle and the same individual manages both the advisory and discretionary relationship. FCA Consumer Duty has reinforced integration by requiring a holistic view of client outcomes across all services delivered. The Advice Guidance Boundary Review (CP23/24) may, in future, create a distinct 'targeted support' tier that warrants a separate capability review, but as of 2025–2026 the regulatory framework is unified. Criteria met: 0 of 4. RETAIN.

sub_capabilities.name: Portfolio Management
sub_capabilities.description: Discretionary management of client investment portfolios: asset allocation, instrument selection, rebalancing, model portfolio construction and maintenance, custody oversight, and MiFID II best execution. Includes both bespoke portfolio management for HNW clients and model portfolio service (MPS) for mass-affluent.

promotion_test.market_evidence: Portfolio Management is the execution arm of the wealth proposition and is deeply integrated with advisory, private banking, and financial planning. The market shows clear commoditisation of portfolio management at the construction layer (passive ETF-based MPS is delivered by Nutmeg, Wealthify, and Vanguard at 0.15–0.75% all-in) but this does not constitute unbundling into a separate capability; it means the commodity layer can be bought via FNZ or SEI platform MPS. Rathbones and Evelyn Partners demonstrate that even at pure-play wealth managers, portfolio management operates as an integrated service line rather than a standalone business unit. The Investment Committee, model portfolio governance, and suitability linkage are inseparable from advisory. BlackRock Aladdin Wealth and Bloomberg PORT exist as specialist tools, but their use does not create a separate organisational capability — they are platform components within Portfolio Management. FCA PROD target market assessment and MiFID II suitability obligations further bind portfolio management to the client advisory process. Criteria met: 0 of 4. RETAIN.

sub_capabilities.name: Private Banking
sub_capabilities.description: Premium relationship banking for HNW and UHNW clients: dedicated relationship managers, personalised credit facilities (portfolio-secured lending, structured credit), FX and international banking, concierge banking services, and integration with the investment and planning relationship. Typically activated above a £500k–£1m liquid assets threshold.

promotion_test.market_evidence: Private Banking in a commercial bank context is the banking layer of the wealth relationship rather than a standalone capability. The structural advantage of a commercial bank over pure-play wealth managers (Rathbones, Brewin Dolphin) is precisely this integration: deposit accounts, credit facilities, FX, and mortgage lending are delivered alongside investment management through a single RM. JP Morgan Private Bank, Coutts (NatWest), and C. Hoare & Co. all demonstrate the integrated model. The credit capability (portfolio-secured lending, Lombard loans) relies on the bank's balance sheet and credit risk framework — it is not a freestanding market capability. FCA regulation of private banking services (deposits under PRA/FCA, lending under Consumer Credit Act where applicable, investment under MiFID II) operates through the same permission set as the broader wealth proposition. The HNW threshold is migrating — industry data suggests effective HNW entry point moving from £250k to £500k+ liquid assets as cost pressures mount — but this is a segmentation change within Wealth Management, not a signal for capability promotion. Criteria met: 0 of 4. RETAIN.

sub_capabilities.name: Financial Planning
sub_capabilities.description: Structured cashflow modelling, retirement planning, tax efficiency analysis, estate planning coordination, and protection gap analysis. Delivers a forward-looking financial plan integrating the client's assets, liabilities, income, expenditure, and goals. Typically delivered by a Chartered Financial Planner alongside or separately from investment management.

promotion_test.market_evidence: Financial Planning is being unbundled in the broader market — fee-only financial planners (e.g. Paradigm Norton, Jacksons Wealth) operate without managing assets, using Voyant or CashCalc as their primary tool — but within a commercial bank wealth arm, financial planning is the anchor that justifies the retained AUM relationship and cross-sells private banking services. Moneyfarm's goals-based digital planning shows the direction of travel for mass-affluent, but at HNW level, cashflow modelling (retirement income, Inheritance Tax planning, trust structuring) is inseparable from the investment mandate. The FCA Retirement Income Review (DP23/3) and the proposed targeted support regime (CP23/24) may create a distinct regulatory category for certain planning activities in future, but as of 2025–2026, financial planning advice is delivered under the same COBS 9A suitability framework as investment advice. The specialist tools (Voyant, CashCalc, Timeline) are buy candidates that sit within the Financial Planning sub-capability — their existence as standalone products does not constitute a capability promotion signal. Criteria met: 0 of 4. RETAIN.

design_decisions.decision: Scope Wealth Management as a single integrated capability encompassing advisory, portfolio management, private banking, and financial planning rather than splitting into separate capabilities.
design_decisions.rationale: The commercial bank's structural moat in wealth is the combination of investment management and banking on a single balance sheet. Splitting into separate capabilities would create integration risk at the deployment boundary — the RM, the suitability process, the client record, and the credit relationship all share state. Every major integrated bank-and-wealth provider (JP Morgan, Coutts, HSBC Private Banking) runs a unified operating model. Consumer Duty's outcomes focus on the holistic client relationship reinforces integration.
alternatives_considered: Promote Financial Planning to a standalone capability (CAP-00X) given the market unbundling trend
Promote Portfolio Management to a standalone capability given commoditisation and buy-vs-build profile
Split Private Banking into a Banking Capability variant for HNW
design_decisions.rejected_because: Financial Planning, Portfolio Management, and Private Banking each scored 0/4 on the promotion test. The unbundling trend in the standalone IFA and robo-advisory market does not translate to a capability split inside a commercial bank where the RM is the single point of relationship and the balance sheet integration is the core differentiator. Splitting would create seams at exactly the point where the bank has competitive advantage.

design_decisions.decision: Mark platform custody and portfolio analytics as 'buy candidates' rather than in-house build components.
design_decisions.rationale: FNZ and SEI have achieved sufficient scale, regulatory track record, and UK market penetration that building proprietary custody infrastructure cannot be justified on cost, speed, or regulatory grounds. BlackRock Aladdin Wealth and Bloomberg PORT for risk analytics are similarly mature. The bank's in-house investment must focus on the client relationship model, suitability orchestration, and balance sheet integration — not commodity platform infrastructure.
alternatives_considered: Build proprietary custody platform to control the data layer
Acquire a wealth platform business (e.g. GBST, Objectway)
design_decisions.rejected_because: Proprietary custody build would take 3–5 years, require significant PRA/FCA capital and operational resilience investment, and deliver no client-facing differentiation. Acquisition of a platform business introduces integration complexity and regulatory change-of-control obligations. FNZ's existing relationships with Lloyds and HSBC demonstrate the viability of the buy route at tier-1 bank scale.

design_decisions.decision: Include the FCA Advice Guidance Boundary Review (CP23/24) as a forward-looking regulatory item requiring a capability review trigger rather than acting on it now.
design_decisions.rationale: If the targeted support regime is enacted, it may create a distinct regulatory channel for digital guidance that sits between execution-only and regulated advice — potentially warranting a new sub-capability or a revision to the Investment Advisory scope. However, as of April 2025 the consultation is still in progress and the final rules are not expected before 2026. Acting on a proposal that may change materially would introduce premature complexity.
alternatives_considered: Pre-emptively create a 'Digital Guidance' sub-capability under CAP-006
Defer the entire capability definition until the regulatory position is settled
design_decisions.rejected_because: Pre-empting draft regulation risks building to a framework that changes. Deferring the entire capability blocks downstream design work. The right response is to document the horizon risk and set a review trigger tied to the FCA policy statement publication.
